content:
Hi everyone! We are happy to share SqueezeBench: a benchmark for Lean-verified bounds on extremal combinatorics problems. We formalize problems in this field as a function f : ℕ → ℕ, and the challenge consists of defining an upper or lower bound on f and proving that (i) it is indeed a bound on f, and (ii) it is strictly better than all previously accepted bounds (not worse at any n, strictly better at some n). This way, we collect an ever-improving set of bounds.

We provide baseline bounds for 10 different problems, obtained with Claude Opus 5, Opus 5.5, and Fable 5.1. As of today, no record is strictly better than already published (not necessarily formalized) bounds in the literature. Once the state of the art is reached for a record, a new submission to SqueezeBench is new mathematics, so its proof could not have been seen by an AI model during training. We will also accept Lean proofs entirely developed by humans, but the usage of AI tools to help with formalization and proofs must be reported.

The functions f under consideration have no known closed form, and are not expected to be found soon. That's why research focuses on finding bounds for those functions. This, together with the fact that submitted bounds always have to be better than the previous ones, makes our benchmark potentially more resilient to saturation than standard benchmarks that only consider closed problems.

We welcome feedback about the formalization of the problems and best practices for maintaining the benchmark. You are also welcome to propose new problems and of course submit some bounds! We plan to process new submissions on a weekly basis. Currently the toolchain is pinned to Lean and Mathlib v4.31.0, and we include a set of tools to check submissions (e.g., Comparator). If we decide to bump the toolchain, we will fix possible issues in the records accordingly.

Repo: https://github.com/leansolving/SqueezeBench
Paper: arXiv:2610.13461

SqueezeBench is joint work with Hai Xia and Stefan Szeider at TU Wien. We look forward to your comments!
